original_question: Let (X, omega) be a compact Hermitian manifold of complex dimension at least 3. Characterize the Hermitian forms omega for which the total volume integral_X (omega + dd^c phi)^n equals integral_X omega^n for every bounded omega-plurisubharmonic function phi.
target_in_paper: Question 29 (Dinew–Kołodziej) in §4.1, "The total volume." It asks to characterize those Hermitian forms ω on compact Hermitian manifolds of complex dimension at least 3 for which ∫_X (ω + dd^c φ)^n = ∫_X ω^n for every bounded ω-plurisubharmonic function φ. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core of the paper’s official formulation almost verbatim: the ambient setting is Hermitian, the dimension restriction is n ≥ 3, the quantifier is universal over bounded ω-plurisubharmonic functions, and the property to be characterized is exactly the invariance of the total Monge–Ampère volume ∫_X (ω + dd^c φ)^n. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
missing_details: The paper is explicitly in the Hermitian/non-Kähler setting: X is a compact complex manifold and ω is the positive (1,1)-form of a Hermitian metric, not just an arbitrary real 2-form. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

To make the question fully stand-alone, one should define what “ω-plurisubharmonic” means in this section: φ is a bounded function on X with ω + dd^c φ ≥ 0 in the sense of currents (the paper introduces this notation immediately before Question 29). ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

The symbol n should be identified explicitly as the complex dimension of X, so that (ω + dd^c φ)^n is the top-degree Monge–Ampère measure integrated over X. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

A fully paper-faithful formulation should note that this is posed as an open characterization problem in the paper, not as a theorem established there. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

The nearby context records a natural candidate condition due to Guan–Li, namely dd^c ω = 0 and dω ∧ d^c ω = 0; this is relevant context, but the paper does not state it as an equivalent reformulation of Question 29. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

The section uses standard dd^c notation without re-fixing the normalization in §4.1, so a completely stand-alone rewrite may either specify the convention or leave dd^c in standard complex-geometric notation. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
refined_question: Let X be a compact complex manifold of complex dimension n ≥ 3, and let ω be the positive (1,1)-form of a Hermitian metric on X (not assumed Kähler). Characterize those Hermitian metrics ω for which the total Monge–Ampère volume is invariant under all bounded ω-plurisubharmonic perturbations, i.e. for which one has ∫_X (ω + dd^c φ)^n = ∫_X ω^n for every bounded upper-semicontinuous function φ on X satisfying ω + dd^c φ ≥ 0 in the sense of currents. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
justification: This is Question 29, not a broader neighboring problem. The surrounding §4 discussion first sets the Hermitian context and explains that, unlike in the Kähler case, the total volume ∫_X (ω + dd^c φ)^n generally depends on φ; Question 29 then asks exactly for a characterization of the forms ω for which that dependence disappears for every bounded ω-psh φ. The next sentence gives the Guan–Li conditions dd^c ω = 0 and dω ∧ d^c ω = 0 only as a “good candidate,” not as a proved equivalence, and §4.2 explains the significance of the problem by noting that the Hermitian Monge–Ampère equation requires an extra normalization constant because total volumes are not generally invariant. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
